rows.quote: In our battery test, which involved continuous web-surfing over Wi-Fi with the display set to 150 nits of brightness, the iPad Pro lasted for 13 hours and 18 minutes.
rows.protocolQuote: The 13-inch iPad Pro that Apple sent us packs an M5 chip with a 10-core CPU, a 10-core GPU, 16GB of RAM and a 1TB SSD.
rows.note: Fallback: Notebookcheck reviewed only the 11-inch M5. Tom's Guide review unit is the 13-inch Wi-Fi + Cellular model, tested over Wi-Fi. Published 21 October 2025 per the page.

rows.quote: Our web browsing workload came in at exactly 10 hours of continuous usage - an improvement compared to the iPad 4. Battery life on LTE was good as well, consistently delivering just under 10 hours of usage. The fact that both LTE and WiFi tests deliver similar results
rows.protocolQuote: We'll start with our 2013 smartphone/tablet web browsing battery life test. As always all displays are calibrated to 200 nits.
rows.note: Fallback: Notebookcheck iPad Air WLAN figure was extrapolated (see rejections). The 10-hour run is the WiFi test (the page contrasts it with the LTE run). Review byline: October 29, 2013. Laptop Mag also has 11h 51min on Wi-Fi at 40 percent brightness (laptopmag.com/reviews/tablets/apple-ipad-air), not added as a row since one fallback outlet is the rule.

rejections.note: Notebookcheck (notebookcheck.com Test-Apple-iPad-Air-1-Tablet.105061, 15.11.2013) box shows 'Surfen über WLAN 9h 13min', but the prose says the scripted WLAN test crashed the browser, so they surfed by hand for 'eine gute Stunde' and extrapolated ('Anschließend haben wir das Ergebnis hochgerechnet'). Not a run to shutdown, so not used; AnandTech (200 nits) used instead.

Notebookcheck (notebookcheck.com Test-Apple-iPad-3rd-Gen-2012-4G-Tablet.71595, 15.03.2012) box shows 'Surfen über WLAN 9h 30min', but the prose calls it 'unsere ersten hochgerechneten Ergebnisse' (extrapolated first results), so not used. AnandTech iPad (2012) review battery page (anandtech.com/show/5688/apple-ipad-2012-review/10, Wayback 20120415) has the 200-nit WiFi result only in a chart image; the text gives only an 8% decrease vs iPad 2 and a max-brightness run (5h 34min), neither usable. Laptop Mag iPad (2012) Verizon review has only an LTE run extrapolated from 4h 34min at 58% left, never updated.
